name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}18 \\ 27\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & 6 & 18 \\ 3 & -3 & -9 & -3 & 27\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 3 & -3 & -9 & -3 & 27\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 & -12 & -9 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -7 & -4 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -4 & 12 \\ -4 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 4
?

Consider the basis B={b1,b2,b3} of the vector space V and the basis C of R2 given by C={[33],[−6−3]}.

Find the matrix [T]B|C of the map T:V→R2 relative to these bases if T(b1)=[3−9],T(b2)=[6−3],T(b3)=[1827].

a
[−7−412−5−38]
b
[−7412−3−34]
c
[−7−412−4−33]
d
[−7−48−4−13]
e
[1−46−435]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that [T]B|C is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1), T(b2), and T(b3) relative to the basis C.

First, we need to find the coordinates of T(bi) relative to the basis C for each i=1,2,3. We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

M=[|||||c1c2T(b1)T(b2)T(b3)|||||].

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

M=[3−636183−3−9−327]R1:=13R1∼[1−21263−3−9−327]R2:=R2−3R1∼[1−212603−12−99]R2:=13R2∼[1−212601−4−33]R2:=R1+2R2∼[10−7−41201−4−33]

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases B and C:

[T]B|C=[−7−412−4−33]
